hypotheses.name: Basement mass-balance residual
hypotheses.physical_signature: Forward-model the broad basement-interface gravity response, fit density contrast on training spatial blocks only, then score persistent transverse gradients of observed-minus-predicted gravity. Freeze the forward model and density fit inside each training fold.
hypotheses.missing_fault_mechanism: A narrow concealed density discontinuity within a basin may remain after removing the broad sediment-thickness response, despite lacking a mapped scarp or catalogue trace.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Lateral sediment-density change or basement-model error; compare the residual against raw gravity and basement-gradient controls, and exclude forward-model edge ringing.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: A physical forward-model residual rather than gravity–magnetic gradient-angle agreement (GMC), scalar gravity-gradient ranking, or radiometric mixing regression.
hypotheses.repository_novelty: No exact forward basement-response subtraction was found in the reviewed local builders/runners. This is a narrow code search only; no claim of novelty across sibling repositories or literature.
hypotheses.expected_dti_potential: Highest qualitative potential in this shortlist because it targets a concealed basin discontinuity rather than a visible surface edge; this is not a numeric score estimate.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Moderate-to-high: verify gravity units/datum and basement conventions, implement fold-contained forward modeling, and compare against raw and compact-source controls.

hypotheses.name: Cross-strike magnetic roughness transition
hypotheses.physical_signature: At label-free magnetic ridges, estimate directional variograms on the two sides of the ridge; score a persistent cross-strike change in roughness exponent and correlation width, not maximum edge amplitude.
hypotheses.missing_fault_mechanism: Distributed fracturing or alteration may change magnetic texture across a damage-zone boundary away from a mapped trace, even when the boundary is not a sharp magnetic step.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Volcanic facies boundaries and survey flight-line noise; require consistency in both magnetic fields, test acquisition-direction periodicity, and compare against non-ridge controls.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: Targets a cross-strike texture-regime change rather than single-pixel worms, Euler depth clusters, contact-offset magnitude, or generic lineament strength.
hypotheses.repository_novelty: No exact two-sided variogram/roughness-transition transform was found in the inspected local builders/runners. Similar texture methods may exist in uninspected sibling repositories; registry-wide novelty is unknown.
hypotheses.expected_dti_potential: Moderate qualitative potential: texture change could extend beyond an edge, but magnetic facies and acquisition artifacts are strong confounders.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Moderate: directional-window choice, variogram fitting, edge conditioning, and flight-line controls require fold-stable validation.
hypotheses.data_availability: Uses competition RTP/TMI channels only if the official bands and units are present in the restored shared cache. No new external raster is required; the shared cache and authenticated official feature file are currently absent.

hypotheses.name: Gravity source-shape consistency
hypotheses.physical_signature: Compare scale-dependent horizontal-to-vertical derivative ratios with a step-source response; suppress compact-source-like responses and score elongated basement-step geometry only when it persists across scales.
hypotheses.missing_fault_mechanism: An extended buried basement step can produce a line-like source response that differs from isolated density bodies, including where the surface catalogue is blank.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Elongate intrusive contacts and basin-margin facies; compare against compact-body and contact controls and test sensitivity to bandwidth and derivative conventions.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: Uses a source-shape likelihood rather than generic gravity-gradient rank, magnetic concordance, or a single derivative threshold.
hypotheses.repository_novelty: The exact step-source-versus-compact-source likelihood was not found in the inspected local builders/runners. This is not a claim of global or literature novelty.

hypotheses.name: Cross-drainage knickzone synchrony
hypotheses.physical_signature: Derive drainage profiles from the elevation surface, locate slope-change points independently along multiple channels, and score only transverse corridors where changes align; reject constant-elevation contour-parallel chains.
hypotheses.missing_fault_mechanism: A concealed active structure could perturb the profiles of several streams along a shared transverse corridor without a mapped fault trace or a single prominent scarp.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Lake shorelines, resistant bedding, roads, and DEM artifacts; compare chain straightness against elevation constancy and lithologic/topographic controls, and reject channels dominated by local engineering.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: Tests multi-channel profile synchrony rather than a LiDAR scarp vote, DEM hinge, generic slope edge, or posterior line filter.
hypotheses.repository_novelty: No exact cross-drainage multi-profile synchrony transform was found in the inspected local builders/runners. A full sibling-repository comparison is unavailable.
hypotheses.expected_dti_potential: Low-to-moderate qualitative potential: independent channel agreement is physically appealing, but the 100 m grid may be too coarse for reliable knickpoint localization.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: High: drainage extraction, profile segmentation, channel independence controls, and robustness to coarse resolution.
